rows.notes: The cited document is a systematic literature review (24 peer-reviewed articles on adoption of drip irrigation in India, 2001-2018); it reports no own field, survey or model data, so Q1 is 'no'. Moreover, its substantive conclusion runs counter to the claim: it argues that mere adoption of micro-irrigation does not automatically result in water conservation because farmers expand irrigated area, raise cropping intensity or shift to water-intensive crops (rebound effect), and that water savings observed on experimental plots cannot be extrapolated to the farm level. Statements about reduced water, fertiliser and energy use are secondary, drawn from the reviewed studies (e.g. Narayanamoorthy 2004b, Kumar 2012, Reddy 2016).
